sessions.title: Greetings and Introductions
sessions.objective: Improve your ability to greet people and introduce yourself confidently.
sessions.can_do: You can greet and introduce yourself and others appropriately in formal and informal settings.
expressions: Pleased to meet you. I'm ___ from ___.
I've heard a lot about you.
How do you pronounce your name?
Let me give you my card.
sessions.language_focus: register choice (formal/informal); introducing third parties; reporting what you've heard
sessions.pronunciation: Name stress; polite intonation; pronouncing unfamiliar names
sessions.task: At a networking mixer, student introduces self, then introduces two strangers to each other; the tutor reacts as a guest with a hard-to-pronounce name. Student = host, Tutor = guest.
sessions.exit_task: Introduces self and others with correct register, handles one name-pronunciation repair, and keeps the exchange moving.
sessions.tutor_notes: Complication: forgot a name. Teach recovery phrases. Names and titles vary across cultures; avoid assumptions about gender or family names.
challenge: Introduce yourself in 20 seconds to a new colleague.
Introduce two people to each other.
Ask someone how to pronounce my name.
repair_phrases: Sorry, I didn't follow. Could you go back a step?
Could you elaborate on that?
I'm not sure I caught the last bit.
Could you slow down a bit?

sessions.language_focus: opening questions; topic bridges; backchannels; closing moves
sessions.pronunciation: Rising-falling intonation to show interest; backchannel sounds
sessions.task: Two acquaintances meet in a break room; the student must open, move between two topics, and exit gracefully. Student = acquaintance, Tutor = acquaintance (who is slightly shy).
sessions.exit_task: Sustains a 2–3 minute conversation with two follow-ups, one topic shift, and a polite close.
sessions.tutor_notes: Complication: the partner gives short answers. Safe-topic norms differ; avoid politics, income, age, and religion unless the partner raises it.
challenge: Start a conversation about the weekend.
Keep it going for one minute using follow-up questions.
Close the conversation politely.
